_note: Frozen commands_with_env() output for the corpus _command-scan-corpus.ts's commandScanCorpus() derives (hooks/_lib/tests/_command-scan-corpus.ts). Each row is {name, command, commands_with_env, raises}: name identifies the row, command is the raw text a hook receives as tool_input.command, commands_with_env is command_scan.py's commands_with_env(command) captured as [[env, tokens], ...] (env an object, tokens a string array), and raises is null unless command_scan.py raises constructing that output, in which case raises holds the exception's type name (e.g. "ValueError") and commands_with_env is null. JSON escaping: command and every token already ran through command_scan.py's _restore(), so a token can carry a raw newline the source text spelled as a real line break (heredoc bodies, a multi-line commit message) or as a backslash-newline line continuation restored back to `\` + newline. Both are written here with JSON's own string escapes: a literal newline is `\n`, and a literal backslash is `\\`, so a restored line continuation appears as the two-character sequence `\\n` (an escaped backslash followed by an escaped newline). No other escaping convention is in play; every other character is JSON's default.
